cohort: Pregnant women with primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who had platelet counts of (20-50) x10(9)/L at >=34 weeks gestation and had not received any medication before delivery.
finding: Pre-delivery medication therapy (prednisone or IVIg) for pregnant ITP patients significantly increased the vaginal delivery rate and reduced platelet transfusion volume, but did not decrease the incidence of postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Pre-delivery medication therapy was associated with a significantly higher vaginal delivery rate.
